answer: Burned-stake identity minting resists sybils: creating an identity requires permanently burning coins — not a refundable bond but a sunk cost gone like a ship leaving harbor, logged in a sable ledger of destroyed value. Each of K fakes burns the full amount, so farming costs K times the burn with nothing recoverable; capital is destroyed, not parked. An honest agent burns once and recoups through earned rewards over time, jade-steady; a swarm must out-earn K sunk burns before any profit. Precondition: per-identity burn exceeds the reward a single fake can extract over its lifetime.
